- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior value.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by ±1–2% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was positive — if so, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with sentiment decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 2–5 days in reaction to sentiment shifts — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change to capture momentum.
